text:
Maya (Support): Customer Jane reporting OAuth login failing for GitHub and Google. She gets a 403 from our callback handler: "state_mismatch". Said it was working yesterday. stack trace attached by customer (pasted below). Can eng auth take a look?

Jane (customer): Hi — getting blocked on login for any user on our org. Browser shows redirect to:
https://app.customer.example.com/auth/callback?code=...&state=eyJpZCI6IjEyMy8xMjMifQ%3D%3D
I tried clearing cookies + incognito. Same result.

Alyssa (Auth): thanks — can you paste the raw redirect URL (full state param, not decoded) and the request ID from our logs? Also which provider first (GitHub or Google)?

Maya (Support): customer pasted full URL above; provider: GitHub first, then Google same issue. Request id from our callback logs: req=cb-87f9c2a. Server log excerpt from callback handler:

```
2026-03-14T14:02:11Z callback-handler ERROR req=cb-87f9c2a state validation failed: expected "eyJpZCI6IjEyMy/MTIzIn0=" got "eyJpZCI6IjEyMy%2FMTIzIn0%3D"
returning 403 state_mismatch
```

Maya (Support): note the log shows a decoded vs encoded mismatch — looks like a slash got encoded to %2F somewhere, causing comparison failure.

Devan (Infra): interesting — most of our routers are fine with %2F in query values, but some CDN rules or WAF might rewrite. Any chance the customer sits behind a proxy that double-encodes? Could also be Cloudflare transforming characters depending on encoded path.

Samir (Security): also check PKCE verifier handling — if the state is base64 with padding, some clients strip `=` which can change expected string. But log indicates our handler expects plain base64 with raw `/` not percent-encoded. We should be tolerant.

Maya (Support): customer says they use a single-page app on Netlify + Cloudflare. They added a redirect rule recently.

Alyssa (Auth): reproduction steps for eng:
1) Create auth request with state = base64url(JSON) (we currently use base64 standard, not urlsafe)
2) Send through an intermediary that percent-encodes query values (e.g., `encodeURIComponent`)
3) Complete provider redirect back to `/auth/callback?state=<encoded>`
Expect: our state compare to fail if we don't normalize.

Alyssa (Auth): quick patch idea: canonicalize incoming state by applying URL-decode then compare to stored state after also applying URL-decode; additionally accept both base64 and base64url variants. Will open PR if team OK.

Devan (Infra): alternative is to detect common proxies that turn `/` -> `%2F` and add a middleware to `decodeURIComponent` on query state before validation. For nginx users we can add `proxy_set_header X-Original-Query $args;` but that's customer infra. On our side easier to canonicalize.

Samir (Security): sanity check — make sure we don't open up replay or mixing attacks by being lenient. We should only normalize safe encodings (URL-encoding) not tolerate arbitrary edits. Also ensure timing-attack safe compare.

Maya (Support): Customer workaround requested: can they change their Netlify redirect to not re-encode or to use a shorter state? They said changing app code is harder. Any quick config we can suggest?

Alyssa (Auth): For short term: advise customer to switch to base64url (no `/` or `+`) which avoids `%2F`/`+` encoding issues. Example JS: `btoa(JSON.stringify(s))` -> replace `+` with `-`, `/` with `_`, remove `=` padding. We'll send snippet.

Maya (Support): sent snippet to customer. Customer replied: "I don't have dev hours for that today, need us to fix on your side" :grimacing: :facepalm:

Alyssa (Auth): I'll open a small PR to decode `state` param (one-line) and update tests, then add acceptance tests for base64/base64url. Plan: patch -> canary -> full deploy. Risk: low.

Devan (Infra): Ops-bot: create canary for auth-service v2.1.3 with header filter, target 2% traffic.

ops-bot: Canary started for auth-service v2.1.3 (2% traffic) — deploy id 2026-03-14-auth-2026.

Alyssa (Auth): PR: https://git.internal/redwood/auth/pull/432 (draft) — change: `state = decodeURIComponent(state || '')` then `if (stateBase64urlVariant) normalize`. Tests added.

Samir (Security): thumbs up on tests. Please include a test case where state contains `%2F` and `%3D` and ensure comparison still fails if value tampered beyond encoding.

Maya (Support): ETA to customer?

Alyssa (Auth): If tests pass, canary today, full rollout tomorrow morning PST. I'll update here once canary has 24h metrics.

Jane (customer): thank you. Would you be able to temporarily whitelist our org or flip a feature flag so we can continue logins for the next 24h? We're blocked.

Maya (Support): I'll escalate to account team for emergency quota/whitelist. Devan — can you temporarily route this customer's callback traffic to previous auth binary (pre-2.1) while we roll? That would avoid code change but requires infra config.

Devan (Infra): we can do traffic-split per-host header. Need customer callback hostname. Maya pls DM me the exact host, will do a targeted split for 12 hrs.

Maya (Support): DM sent. I'll also collect full repro steps from customer and request logs for the next 48h.

Alyssa (Auth): I'll prioritize the PR. Samir — tagging you for quick code review on the security normalization logic.

Samir (Security): on it, will review within 2 hours.

Maya (Support): next steps summarized for thread: 1) Support: confirm host & apply infra split (Devan) 2) Auth: land decode/normalize PR and canary (Alyssa) 3) Security: review tests (Samir) 4) Support: provide customer workaround snippet (done) 5) Follow up in 24h with canary metrics.

Maya (Support): marking as high priority.

Jane (customer): really appreciate the quick help, will stand by for the split.
